subject: Cross-border routing and export controls - residency & deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@fintechco.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: question on where requests are processed and export controls

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. To close our internal review we need a concise answer to two items so our security and procurement teams can proceed:

1) For API requests sent to Redwood's hosted API, in which cloud regions can request processing and KV/prefix caches occur? In particular, do any parts of the request or cache ever leave the US for routing or batch processing?

2) For customers operating in EMEA under our contract, what controls does Redwood provide to prevent export of EU-origin data to non-EU territories? Do you have a summary of subprocessors and any export-control attestations?

We're trying to map this into our procurement checklist. If you can share a short mapping and any evidence pointers (architectural diagram, subprocessors list), that'd be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Security & Privacy Lead
FinTechCo
alice.nguyen@fintechco.com
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: question on where requests are processed and export controls

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front, then a bit of detail: 

1) Hosted API processing regions: requests are processed in the customer-selected region where available. For US customers we route to US regions (primary: us-west-2, fallback: us-east-1). Prefix/KV caching is colocated with the chosen serving pool and does not persistently move across regions unless a failover occurs per the routing policy (we document failover paths).

2) EMEA controls: we offer EU-hosted endpoints (europe-west2 / frankfurt availability). When a customer selects an EU-residency configuration, request processing, KV caches, and short-term artifacts remain within EU-hosted clusters by default. Cross-border export is only possible via explicit routing policies (e.g., legacy customers with hybrid setups) and otherwise requires customer opt-in or a documented failover/incident where we escalate for approval.

I'll loop in Rishi with the processing topology and subprocessors inventory; he can add specifics about which subprocessor locations and network hops are involved. Attaching a short summary next message.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive — Compliance & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@fintechco.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: question on where requests are processed and export controls

Hi Alice, adding the technical detail you asked for — I kept it focused for procurement/security review.

Processing and routing:
- Regional serving pools: primary serving happens in cloud regions selected at onboarding. Common defaults: AWS us-west-2 (US West), AWS us-east-1 (US East), GCP europe-west2 (Frankfurt), and GCP europe-west1 (Belgium) where available.
- Smart routing: requests are routed by policy (latency, cost, region). For EU-residency customers, routing policies restrict to EU pools; non-EU pools are excluded unless a customer-configured failover is activated.
- Cache behaviour: in-session KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and stored on the same region's serving nodes. We do not replicate KV caches across regions except during an explicit cross-region failover event.

Subprocessors (high level):
- Core compute: AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1), GCP (europe-west2), and selected partner bare-metal farms for Dedicated customers.
- Storage/logging: encrypted short-term logs are stored in regionally scoped buckets (we rotate and purge per retention policy). Long-term analytics buckets may be configured in a separate region only with customer consent.
- Networking & CDN: FastPath CDN (edge nodes globally) for static assets; edge nodes do not persist request bodies. Edge hops are TLS-encrypted and do not store PII.

Export controls & evidence pointers:
- We provide a subprocessor inventory CSV on request (names, service, primary regions).
- We maintain a processing topology diagram (link below) that maps where tokens, request bodies, caches, and logs live for each deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private).
- In cases requiring strict export controls we recommend either: 1) EU-only Dedicated pools, or 2) Redwood Private (VPC) with on-prem options — both avoid exporting processing outside EU.

If you want, I can produce a short two-page exhibit that maps your typical API call to the exact services/hops. That usually satisfies procurement evidence requests.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial: question on where requests are processed and export controls

Alice — attaching the two artifacts we discussed to help you map into procurement:

Attachments: 1) redwood-dataflow-map.pdf — high-level processing topology for hosted vs dedicated vs private; 2) export-controls-matrix.xlsx — list of subprocessors, primary regions, and compliance notes.

A few callouts for your checklist:
- Default: Hosted API respects customer region selection; EU-hosted configuration keeps processing and ephemeral caches in EU pools.
- Failover: Cross-region failover is documented and requires a trigger; in most contracts we make this an opt-in behavior for residency-sensitive customers.
- Deletion: Short-lived artifacts (KV/prefix cache) are kept for session duration and purged on session termination; logs follow the retention timeline in our DPA (we can provide a time-stamped export).

If procurement/security need signed evidence (SOC2 or subprocessors attestation), let me know and I will queue the request with our compliance team — we can provide dated inventory CSV + SOC2 summary under NDA.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Account Executive — Compliance & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
